identity.title: Dust-depleted Inner Disks in a Large Sample of Transition Disks through Long-baseline ALMA Observations

paper_type_evidence.quote: we have collected ALMA archival continuum observations of 38 transition disks with resolved dust cavities, for which we have measured the size and dust mass of the inner disk, or placed upper limits.

question.value: Do transition disk cavities host inner mm-dust disks, and what are their sizes, dust masses, orientations and depletion relative to the outer disk?

evidence.quote: We present a high resolution continuum study of inner disks in the cavities of 38 transition disks.
lower resolution Band 7 data (program 2012.1.00303.S) were used to measure the surface density profile of the outer disk

method.value: Detection above 3x RMS at stellar location; Gaussian fit with imfit; otherwise 3 RMS upper limit; R_inner = HWHM or largest ellipse fitting in beam if unresolved

evidence.quote: A detection is defined as the measurement of a flux at the stellar location above a threshold of 3 times the RMS image noise level.

assumptions.value: Unresolved inner disks have same inclination and PA as outer disk

evidence.quote: where unresolved, we assume the inner disk has the same inclination and position angle as the outer disk
For each of the 18 detections, a Gaussian model is fit using the CASA `imfit` task.

method.value: Optically thin Rayleigh-Jeans flux with passively heated flared disk T(r), Sigma_d propto 1/r, between R_sub and R_inner

evidence.quote: This means that the mm-dust mass can computed accurately with the optically thin assumption.

key_parameters.value: flaring angle 0.02; R_sub=0.07 sqrt(L*) au; kappa 10 cm2/g at 1000 GHz, beta=1; assumed R_inner=5 au for unresolved

evidence.quote: with $\sigma_B$ the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, $\phi$ the flaring angle (taken as 0.02) and $L_*$ the stellar luminosity.
in this approach using the blackbody approximation we ignore scattering, which might result in an underestimate of the inner disk dust mass

validation.value: Optical depth checked against expected thick/thin flux vs L*

evidence.quote: First, we check the optical depth by estimating the expected flux based on basic radiative transfer calculations, given the stellar luminosity.

analysis_steps.goal: Build dust surface density profiles and delta_dust

method.value: R_cav from azimuthally averaged profile; R_outer from curve-of-growth at 95% flux; delta_dust is inner/outer surface density ratio

evidence.quote: successively larger photometric apertures are applied until the measured flux is 95% of the total flux

fitting.value: Gaussian ring chi2 fit for 7 outer disks lacking orientation

evidence.quote: a $\chi^2$ minimization with steps of 0.005" in radial direction and 1$^{\circ}$ results in the best fit values
Our derived values for $R_\text{cav}$ are generally within 20% of the literature values

findings_qualitative.value: Inner mm-dust disks are depleted relative to outer disks, uncorrelated with accretion rate and NIR excess

evidence.quote: The near-infrared excess is uncorrelated with the mm dust mass of the inner disk.

claims.hypothesis: Inner disks in transition disk cavities are frequently misaligned
claims.experiment: Compare inclination/PA of resolved inner and outer disks

evidence.quote: Of the 14 resolved disks, 8 are significantly misaligned with the outer disk.

claims.hypothesis: NIR excess traces mm inner dust
claims.experiment: Regression of dust mass vs NIR excess
claims.finding: NIR excess is not a reliable tracer

evidence.quote: we find no significant correlation between these properties

claims.hypothesis: Inner disks follow the size-luminosity relation

evidence.quote: this is only slightly offset but with a slope that is consistent with the results of (cite: Andrews2018size)

claims.hypothesis: PDS 70 inner disk differs because planets recently opened the gap
claims.result: PDS 70 and WSB 60 have large inner disks and xi~100

evidence.quote: We propose the hypothesis that PDS 70b has only recently formed and opened a gap in the disk

why_this_data.value: Archival data chosen to best resolve the dust cavity and inner disk

evidence.quote: The archival ALMA data collected for each disk was chosen in order to best resolve the dust cavity and inner disk (if present).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Free-free jet emission as alternative to inner dust disk, not ruled out

evidence.quote: One other explanation for apparent misalignment of the inner disk in the millimeter is that we are not measuring inner disk dust emission, but free-free emission from a jet

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity non-uniform so occurrence is likely underestimated; sample biased toward large bright disks

evidence.quote: As our sensitivity is extremely non-uniform across the sample, this is likely an underestimate of the occurrence rate of inner disks.

referee_caveats_inferred: Blackbody optically thin mass with fixed phi=0.02 and kappa ignores scattering and uncertain temperatures
Gas-to-dust inference relies on alpha-disk assumption and literature accretion rates with 0.5 dex error
Heterogeneous images (weighting chosen to maximize inner disk S/N) bias detections
Inner disk size from Gaussian fits near beam size is uncertain
